title: A cloud container cannot reach the Actions API at all, and `fleet-token.mjs` reports that blocked route as a platform refusal — the one environment the fallback was built for is the one where its error reads as a permissions problem
body:
## What happened

`fleet-token.mjs` resolves its three inputs from the environment first and, for whatever the environment lacks, from the board repository's Actions variables. That fallback was verified on a maintainer workstation. It was never verified inside a fleet cloud container, which is the environment it exists for.

A PM seat running in one reported this, from a container whose credential is perfectly good:

```
node scripts/pm/fleet-token.mjs --print
✗ GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/variables/OS_FLEET_APP_ID
  → HTTP 403 Access to this GitHub Actions path is not permitted through this proxy.
exit 3 (PREREQUISITE)
```

`through this proxy` is the egress proxy's own wording, not the platform's. The container reaches `/repos/{o}/{r}/issues/…` with the same credential; it is the `/repos/*/actions/*` path class that is refused. The seat read the source, reached the right conclusion unaided, and correctly declined to work around the proxy — but only after spending a round on it, because the message it was handed describes a credential or permission problem and the cause is network policy.

Independently confirmed: Claude Code's cloud egress proxy special-cases github.com at the host level, and an environment's own network-access allowlist does not override it (anthropics/claude-code#86828, closed as not planned). So this is not a transient condition and not something a repository setting can lift.

## Why this is a defect worth fixing rather than a note in a header

The three shapes below are indistinguishable in today's output, and they call for three different actions:

| cause | what the user must do |
|:--|:--|
| the token cannot read the variable | fix the credential or the variable's visibility |
| the variable does not exist | `gh variable set …` |
| **this environment cannot reach the Actions API at all** | **stop using this route; inject the three environment variables** |

Only the third is common in the fleet, and it is the one the message does not name. A tool that hands a seat the wrong remedy costs a round every time a new container meets it, and every fleet container will meet it.

There is a second, smaller mis-signal behind it: a 403 carrying no `x-ratelimit-remaining` header is classified `ratelimit` by `classifyHttp`, because `Number(null) === 0`. The exit code that results is right by accident (3, prerequisite) but the reasoning is not, and a future reader of that path will be misled.

## The fix

1. **Recognise the shape.** When a variables read answers 403 and the body or status line carries the proxy's own marker (the `through this proxy` wording, or any 403 on the `/repos/*/actions/` prefix that is not accompanied by a GitHub error body), report it as *this environment cannot reach the Actions API*, and prescribe the remedy that applies: set `OS_FLEET_APP_ID`, `OS_FLEET_INSTALLATION_ID` and `OS_FLEET_PRIVATE_KEY` in the environment, and `OS_FLEET_INPUTS_FROM_GITHUB=0` to close the route so the next failure names the missing variable instead.
2. **Say where the inputs may live**, in that same message: the environment (primary), or the board repository's Actions variables (fallback, unavailable in environments whose egress proxy refuses the path class).
3. **Do not widen `classifyHttp`.** Its `ratelimit` arm reading a header-less 403 as exhausted is a separate finding; this card must not paper over it by adding a branch that happens to mask it. Pin the distinction instead.

## Acceptance

- A 403 of the proxy's shape produces a message naming the environment-variable remedy and `OS_FLEET_INPUTS_FROM_GITHUB=0`, with the exit code unchanged at 3.
- A genuine GitHub 403 (a real error body, no proxy marker) still reports as a platform refusal and does NOT suggest the environment-variable remedy — both directions pinned in `--self-test`, because a recogniser that fires on everything is the same defect facing the other way.
- The self-test drives both through a fake platform; ⛔ no network.
- The header states that the variables route is unavailable behind an egress proxy that refuses the `/repos/*/actions/` class, and names the environment as the route that always works.
- ⛔ Out of scope: `classifyHttp`'s header-less-403 arm, and any attempt to work around the proxy.
